precepts.text: The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel, his thoughts like a rolling axletree: three is one, one is three, in circles without end.
precepts.point: If a wise man contends with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh there is no rest: it is a circular argument that goes nowhere.

note.label: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.why:
“If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man”: if a wise man debates with a stupid man or woman. And “whether he rage or laugh”: whether that fool laughs at it or is angry at it, “there is no rest.” There is no conclusion. It is a circular argument; you argue the same thing over and over again and it goes nowhere.

Sirach shows why: “The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.” The fool is a circular idiot. His mind just goes in circles, nonstop. That is the Trinity man: three is one, one is three, they are all the same, the Father and the Son of one substance. Round and round, and you cannot win. They are dead set in it, their minds sealed as with a hot iron.

Show them that the Father has sons, the children of Israel, and they cannot understand it: no, they are all one. Stump them in a debate and they keep going: but what about this? It is ongoing. It is a cartwheel. They will not yield to reason. Even the German had some sense when he called insanity doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.

So leave that negro alone. You are wasting your time. These are unreasonable people, and you have to let them go. The wise man who keeps contending with the fool gets no rest, because the fool's heart only rolls in circles of nonsense.

precepts.text: He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy. Corrected over and over, and after a while the neck hardens, the scriptures have no effect, there is no contriteness, no shame. If the word of God is not moving you to change after ten years, something is disconnected. The word of God changes you; if it is not working, examine whether you even believe.
precepts.point: But if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes: definition read in class, forsake means to abandon, desert, or leave entirely, a breach of duty. Then will I pluck them up by the roots, and make them to be a proverb and a byword among all nations. Reading that is understanding why we went into captivity.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.” Often reproved means every time the correction comes, he will not accept it. So he gets corrected over and over, and after a while his neck becomes hardened. He becomes stiffnecked. The scriptures don't have that effect on him anymore; there is no contriteness, no shame. You see brothers always getting stood up, and after a while it's, yeah, okay, put me out, I'll be back.

Why does that happen? The word of God is not moving you to change. You can't be the same person you were before; there has to be some type of growth. How do you find yourself doing the same thing you were doing ten years ago? Why, ten years later, does somebody have to motivate you to go do the work? Something is not firing off; something is disconnected.

The word of God is supposed to inspire you to change. The word of God changes you; the word of God can cure you. If you ain't changing, it is one of two things: you are a heathen, or you are a reprobate, and the kingdom ain't for you. So if it is not working, examine whether you even believe.

That is the other side of 2 Chronicles 7:14. The Lord will hear and forgive and heal the land when his people humble themselves and turn from their wicked ways. The one who hardens his neck against reproof is suddenly destroyed, and that without remedy.

precepts.text: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not. He keeps it tucked in, which goes against Leviticus 5.
precepts.point: But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon's faction murders were committed: Simon hated Onias so much he had one of his men kill one of Onias's priests. That is why I say it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
“This Simon now, of whom we spake afore, having been a betrayer of the money, and of his country, slandered Onias”. Simon of the tribe of Benjamin revealed the secret of the money to the Greeks and then slandered Onias the third, telling them Onias was the one who did that to Heliodorus. This Simon was no damn good.

Now look at the ones who stand next to that kind of man: “Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not.”

The type of man who is a partner with it hates his own soul. He hears the cursing and does not tell it. He keeps it tucked in. That goes directly against the law in Leviticus 5, where the one who hears and does not utter it bears the iniquity.

So it is not only the Simon who is guilty. The one who stands by, hears the evil, and keeps quiet is partnered with him, and he is hating his own soul.

precepts.text: Where there is no vision, the people perish. Early on there was really no direction in the other camps: talking crazy in the streets with no plan. Whose congregation is thriving with hating the black woman and hating the nations as the basis of their teaching?
precepts.point: On the 501c3 accusation: a 501c3 is just a tax classification, meaning we do not pay tax; when we spend at the store we keep the tax money and buy more unleavened bread. It is not a check that gets cut. And if you think we had to stop teaching the commandments and faith in Christ for it, look what we are teaching; nobody cut the feed and nobody cut the funding.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
“Where there is no vision, the people perish”. Early on there was really no direction in the other camps. In 2006 one of the biggest things taught was that 9/11 was an inside job. Israelites were doing hour-long videos on the back of the dollar bill: connect the words, it says Mason on it. There was FEMA camp doctrine, that we were all going to get killed and put in plastic coffins at Walmart. People were scared to go to Walmart. Their focus wasn't on the right thing.

Some brothers said, we're going to take to the streets and talk crazy to white folks and at the women as they walk by. Where has that gotten them today? Who grew a congregation by hating the black woman, the white man and all the other nations? Whose congregation is thriving with that as the basis of its teaching?

The Nathaniel 7 page separated many so-called teachers from those who actually feared God and understood the mission. Having a vision, a plan for our people and for the kingdom, is part of the foundation laid on Christ. Without it, the work burns and the people perish.

precepts.text: He that being often reproved hardeneth his neck: corrected until correction is void, then bitter, then out the door with wife and children.
precepts.point: For one morsel of meat he sold his birthright: your trinkets are a morsel of meat, and afterward Esau was rejected and found no place of repentance though he sought it with tears. That will be many bitter brothers and sisters in that day, and Christ will say I never knew thee.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
Hebrews warns “lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you”. Where does that root come from? Proverbs answers: “He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck”. He that is often corrected hardens his neck, meaning his mind. You can't tell that brother nothing: I'm a man, you a man, I do what I want. Well, do what you want and burn by yourself.

That is the mindset of a lot of our brothers and sisters. They never took the scripture serious. Leadership corrects them, corrects them, corrects them, to the point where the correction is null and void, because they are not going to apply anything. After a while the Lord says, this spirit is rebellious as hell; he always hardens his mind and doesn't give a damn what you're saying.

You end up hardening your heart from always having correction done to you, until at the end of the day bitterness is formed, and then you're out the door with your wife and your children.

So the question for every brother and sister: are you one of the many that shall be offended when correction comes, when the men are told to get their homes in order and the women to be that pillar of rest and not stress? Or will you get in check with the Lord? The bitterness of Hebrews 12 grows out of a neck hardened against reproof.

precepts.text: Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss. Around the right people, when tempted you think it through, remember the judgment, and the fear activates.
precepts.point: Romans 6:16-19: to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are. Fall into sin and you worship the devil in that moment; you cannot serve two masters. As ye yielded your members to uncleanness, now yield them to righteousness unto holiness. Satan says you fell and cannot get up; you can repent, that is why Christ came.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.” A hasty man acts off of impulse, and the answer to that is not to act off of impulse but to think it through: “Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss.”

Whatever we take in hand, we remember the end. We have to be in that frame of mind, and we have to be around the right people, being around the righteous and staying occupied in the work. Whoever commits sin while being around the righteous family, Satan is heavy on him.

So when we are tempted, we can think things through and remember the judgment of the Lord, and the fear activates, and then we can overcome.

That is the whole choice set out in Romans 6: “Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” Fall into sin and in that moment you are serving the devil, because you cannot have two masters. Remembering the end is how a hasty man learns patience, resolve and discipline.

precepts.text: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you. Not occupied in the work and the study, bitterness springs up; separate from your people and Satan plays on your psyche: they never liked you anyway. 1 Peter 5:8, be sober and vigilant, for the devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, as he desired to sift Peter.
precepts.point: Romans 6:16-19: to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are. Fall into sin and you worship the devil in that moment; you cannot serve two masters. As ye yielded your members to uncleanness, now yield them to righteousness unto holiness. Satan says you fell and cannot get up; you can repent, that is why Christ came.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God.” We have to be diligent, constantly abounding in the work, because if we are not, we can fall from the grace of God.

“lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you.” If you are not occupied in doing the Lord’s work, not putting your hands to the plow, not studying, not being amongst the righteous, a root of bitterness can spring up in you, because you are not studying to combat it. You might have a feeling, but you had better rebuke that thing, and the way to do it is to be around these people.

If you draw back and separate from your people, Satan has you right where he wants you. Now he can play on your psyche and your mind. When you are not constantly seeing people you start thinking differently: they never liked you anyway. That is what Satan does.

“Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.” Satan wants to devour all of us, just as Christ told Peter that Satan desired to have him to sift him as wheat. We have to be in that mindset and know what is going on. The hasty man who does not look diligently lets bitterness spring up, and he is worse off than a fool.

precepts.text: A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will. Do not hear a class like this and say that ain't it; that is the excuse to go back to your pleasure. Sirach 6:4, a wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it and make him laughed to scorn of his enemies. Sirach 27:3, unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.
precepts.point: Romans 6:16-19: to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are. Fall into sin and you worship the devil in that moment; you cannot serve two masters. As ye yielded your members to uncleanness, now yield them to righteousness unto holiness. Satan says you fell and cannot get up; you can repent, that is why Christ came.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” When you hear a class like this, do not say, Oh, that ain’t it. You are just making an excuse to go back to your pleasure and your lust, to feel comfortable in them.

The excuse maker starts a fight over the chicken so he can leave and get some duck. It is like the story the Bishop told about the co-worker who dealt with multiple women and would start a fight with one to go see the other. Now you are pointing the finger at everybody else, when back at the ranch you really want to go have fun in your pleasure and your lust. As the Bishop’s graphic says, a sin-filled soul will find and make excuses only to fulfill its lust. That is very dangerous.

“A wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorn of his enemies.” And “Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.”

So we have to have fear and we have to be diligent if we want a fighting chance. The man hasty in his words, who always has an excuse ready, will not be reproved, and that is why there is more hope of a fool than of him.

precepts.text: Who will set scourges over my thoughts and the discipline of wisdom over my heart, that they spare me not for my ignorances? Wisdom of Solomon 6:17, the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline, and the care of discipline is love. Ephesians 6:11, put on the whole armour; if you are not studying you are not battling, only falling victim.
precepts.point: Romans 6:16-19: to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are. Fall into sin and you worship the devil in that moment; you cannot serve two masters. As ye yielded your members to uncleanness, now yield them to righteousness unto holiness. Satan says you fell and cannot get up; you can repent, that is why Christ came.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
The hasty man needs control, and control comes by discipline: “Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins.” We have to learn discipline so we do not end up looking crazy out here.

“For the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline; and the care of discipline is love.” The very true beginning of following after wisdom is the desire of discipline. So we have to fight temptation, fight off the devil and overcome the beast in order to learn that discipline.

“Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.” We have to put on all of the armour. If you are not studying, you are not battling; you are just falling victim.

Keeping God’s commandments does not give instant gratification. The consequences are delayed: we are going to get the kingdom. Sin gives you the pleasure right then and there, the instant dopamine, and once you are hardened by the deceitfulness of sin you no longer see any reason to keep God’s commandments because they do nothing for you in the moment. In this truth you have to self-motivate. You cannot wait for somebody else to give you a pep talk. You have to discipline your own soul if you want to make it.

precepts.text: So shall righteousness hate iniquity when she decketh herself, and shall accuse her to her face; the Lord defends him that diligently searcheth out every sin. Discipline your mind to hate iniquity. Wisdom of Solomon 5:13-15: the hope of the ungodly is dust blown away and the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day, but the righteous live for evermore and their reward is with the Lord. Do the homework and you live forever while the instant feelings pass.
precepts.point: Romans 6:16-19: to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are. Fall into sin and you worship the devil in that moment; you cannot serve two masters. As ye yielded your members to uncleanness, now yield them to righteousness unto holiness. Satan says you fell and cannot get up; you can repent, that is why Christ came.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“So shall righteousness hate iniquity, when she decketh herself, and shall accuse her to her face, when he cometh that shall defend him that diligently searcheth out every sin upon earth.” We have to learn to hate iniquity. We have to discipline our minds to hate iniquity and to hate sin. If we want the Lord to defend us, that is what we have to do.

Wisdom of Solomon shows the end of both sides. The ungodly say, “Even so we in like manner, as soon as we were born, began to draw to our end, and had no sign of virtue to shew; but were consumed in our own wickedness.” The hope of the ungodly “is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.”

“But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.” You may not see it right now, but if you keep God’s commandments, if you do the homework, you are going to live forever, while everything that feels good in the moment passes away. The Most High cares for you, if you are able to hate sin.

That is the answer to the hasty man: discipline the mind to hate iniquity, and the Lord defends the one who diligently searches out every sin.

precepts.text: A man's pride shall bring him low, but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.
precepts.point: Forgive, lest Satan should get an advantage of us, for we are not ignorant of his devices. Examine whether a subtle pride is his device on you: not asking for help, thinking too highly of yourself, refusing correction. Captain Matthew adds that pride is also why a heavy brother will not change his eating.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Look what pride does: “A man’s pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.” Pride is one of Satan's devices, and it does not have to be loud and in your face. It can be subtle. Sometimes it shuts you down, I can do this on my own, I don't need anybody, and it always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. Pride destroyed us in the kingdom, and it can keep destroying us right now.

Pride destroyed every kingdom on the earth. The king of Assyria sent his messenger with big words against Hezekiah and the Lord, and the angel of the Lord smote a hundred fourscore and five thousand in one night; then his own sons killed Sennacherib with the sword while he worshipped his god. Nebuchadnezzar said, is not this great Babylon, built by the might of my power, and while the word was in his mouth the kingdom departed from him, and he ate grass as oxen until he knew that the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men. Antiochus spoke proudly and was smitten with a remedyless pain of the bowels. Herod took the glory of a god and was eaten of worms.

No kingdom is exempt, not Assyria, Babylon, Greece, Rome or America. And none is more prideful than Edom, the white man, of whom it is written, the pride of thine heart hath deceived thee.

But honour upholds the humble in spirit. Nebuchadnezzar humbled himself and came back saying there is no God like the God of Daniel. David humbled himself and God called him a man after his own heart. The only way our kingdom will last forever is to walk in wisdom and humility towards God; outside of that, pride brings us low like every nation before us.

precepts.text: The rod and reproof give wisdom, so there is a structure to discipline in the home. And "where there is no vision the people perish" is not only the body — as the man of the house you dictate the vision, and some of you have to ask whether you ever set one.
precepts.point: Daughters marry what their fathers were, and sons become the kind of father and husband you are. If you were a tyrant or a drunkard, that is the quality she will look for and how he will move.

note.label: To Whom Much Is Given: The Burden and Beauty of Godly Leadership

precepts.text: The fear of man bringeth a snare, but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe; if you fear what the people will say, you will fall into the trap and transgress, which is why a leader cannot fold when the people become too much to handle; Saul would have been safe had he trusted the Lord.
precepts.point: Then he asks, Pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship the Lord; take me back to the regular Saul and Samuel connection, as though a fearful excuse settles it.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
Now the confession finally comes, and it is still not sincere: “I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.” Even in admitting it he deflects: it is the fault of the wicked people you put me over. Then he asks, “pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship the Lord”: take me back to the regular Saul and Samuel connection, as though a fearful excuse settles it.

“The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe.” If you fear what the people will say, you will fall into the trap and transgress. That is why a leader cannot fold when the people become too much to handle. Saul would have been safe had he trusted the Lord.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 22

precepts.why: “An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked”: this is why the wicked despise Israel United in Christ and try to bring us down any chance they get.
